question: As part of handing off an agent to a customer's compliance team, the vendor needs the receiving team to have a record of every file the agent modifies once it is running unattended. Which mechanism should be included in the handoff?
options: A) A README file that describes, in general terms, the categories of files the agent is expected to touch
B) A nightly script that re-reads the entire repository to guess which files might have changed
C) A SessionStart hook that prints the agent's configuration once when the session begins
D) A PostToolUse hook that writes an audit-log entry each time an Edit or Write tool call completes
correct_answers: D) A PostToolUse hook that writes an audit-log entry each time an Edit or Write tool call completes
explanations: A general README describes expected behavior but does not produce a record of what the agent actually did during unattended runs.
Re-scanning the repository after the fact can detect that files changed but cannot reliably attribute each change to a specific tool call.
A SessionStart hook only fires once at session initialization, so it cannot capture individual file modifications made afterward.
Correct - a PostToolUse hook matched on Edit and Write fires after each modification, giving the compliance team a reliable, per-change audit record.
